subject: Kathryn Bigelow
hook: She beat her ex-husband's blockbuster for Best Director.
twist: The ex-husband she beat for Best Director says he was the first on his feet applauding her.
mood: Desert-dust military field-notebook: sun-bleached ochre, khaki, faded olive and rust-red stamp ink on grainy graph paper, with pencil sketches, coffee rings, taped tickets and typed field-report labels. Music: sparse, tense desert-blues underscore, slow 70 bpm, dry guitar twang, low frame drum and ticking pulse, resolving to a single warm sustained chord at the twist.
narration: She beat her ex-husband's blockbuster for Best Director. March seventh, twenty ten. Kathryn Bigelow had made The Hurt Locker, a war film about a bomb disposal team in Iraq. It cost about fifteen million dollars. Avatar, from her former husband James Cameron, had already earned over two billion. Barbra Streisand opened the envelope. "Well, the time has come," she said. Bigelow became the first woman ever to win Best Director. Her film also won Best Picture, though it had made only around fifteen million dollars at the American box office. Avatar took three awards: art direction, cinematography and visual effects. Cameron was sitting right behind her. He later told the New York Times he was "the first one on my feet applauding." The man she beat, by his own account, stood up first.

She beat her ex-husband's blockbuster for Best Director. 🎬

March 2010. Kathryn Bigelow's The Hurt Locker, a war film about a bomb disposal team, cost about fifteen million dollars. Avatar, from her former husband James Cameron, had already earned over two billion.

Barbra Streisand opened the envelope: "Well, the time has come." Bigelow became the first woman in the Academy's eighty-two years to win Best Director, and her film took Best Picture too, with only around fifteen million dollars at the American box office.

The twist: Cameron was sitting right behind her. He later told the New York Times he was "the first one on my feet applauding."
